question: What main factor sets maritime nursing apart from working in a hospital?

options.A: Having immediate access to surgical specialists
options.B: Following national hospital safety guidelines only
options.C: Working independently with limited medical resources
options.D: Treating exclusively pediatric patients during voyages

explanation: Maritime nurses operate far from traditional hospital infrastructure and must rely on their own skills and finite supplies. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h1)

question: Why is knowing international health rules important for a nurse working on a ship?

options.A: Ships frequently cross borders and must comply with global maritime health rules
options.B: Global health rules prevent any infectious diseases from ever entering a vessel
options.C: It allows nurses to bypass local hospital admission fees completely
options.D: International law requires nurses to act as ship captains

explanation: Vessels travel through various international jurisdictions, requiring adherence to standardized maritime health protocols. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h1)

question: The constant movement of a ship means boat nurses must focus on which key physical skill?

options.A: Predicting exact weather patterns using nautical charts
options.B: Operating large marine diesel engines during emergencies
options.C: Designing larger medical bay expansions on cargo vessels
options.D: Maintaining physical stability while performing clinical procedures

explanation: Constant vessel motion forces nurses to anchor themselves securely to deliver safe patient care. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h2)

question: How do environmental conditions like humidity and salt spray affect medical supplies on a ship?

options.A: They automatically sterilize all surgical instruments on board
options.B: They have no impact on modern medical gear or pharmaceuticals
options.C: They extend the active shelf life of injectable medications
options.D: They can degrade sterile packaging and damage equipment faster

explanation: Harsh maritime climates accelerate wear and tear on medical packaging and sensitive diagnostic devices. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which systematic approach is best for a boat nurse to use during an initial patient check?
explanation: The ABCDE method remains the standard framework for identifying immediate life-threatening conditions in any emergency. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h3)

question: Why is continuous vital sign monitoring so important during patient assessment at sea?

options.A: Maritime law requires exact numeric logs every five minutes
options.B: Ship engines interfere with electronic monitors if not checked hourly
options.C: Evacuation is often delayed, requiring prolonged management of changing conditions
options.D: Patients recover much faster when watched continuously by two nurses

explanation: Because help is far away, the nurse must watch closely for subtle signs of patient deterioration over time. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the top trauma priority when caring for an injured crew member at sea?

options.A: Documenting the exact wind speed during the incident
options.B: Controlling massive hemorrhage and managing the airway
options.C: Administering oral antibiotics to prevent marine infections
options.D: Performing a complete neurological reflex examination

explanation: Stopping severe bleeding and ensuring a patent airway are the foundational steps of immediate trauma life support. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h4)

question: How does performing CPR on a moving ship differ from doing it in a hospital?

options.A: It is completely automated by ship stabilization systems
options.B: It eliminates the need for chest compressions entirely
options.C: It can only be performed while the ship is docked in port
options.D: It requires physical endurance and utilizing untrained crew members for assistance

explanation: The unstable environment and small team size force nurses to rely on available crew for active resuscitation help. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h4)

question: What tool allows boat nurses to consult directly with doctors on land?
explanation: Telehealth links the vessel's medical bay with land-based doctors for expert guidance during complex cases. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h5)

question: Why is keeping strict inventory of the ship's medical chest essential?

options.A: Crew members frequently consume emergency drugs for minor headaches
options.B: Medicines expire faster when stored inside metal ship hulls
options.C: Running out of critical supplies mid-ocean puts patient lives at high risk
options.D: International ports fine ships that carry extra bandages

explanation: Resupply is impossible while far out at sea, making careful stock tracking a life-or-death necessity. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h5)

question: What crucial details must a boat nurse provide when calling for a helicopter evacuation?

options.A: The exact brand of the ship's engine
options.B: The personal background of the ship captain
options.C: A complete inventory of the galley food supply
options.D: GPS coordinates and current patient status

explanation: Rescue teams need exact positioning and clinical severity to dispatch the correct air or sea rescue assets. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h6)

question: Why must medical tubes and lines be secured extra carefully before a helicopter hoist transfer?

options.A: Aviation rules forbid any medical lines during flight operations
options.B: Rotor wash and turbulent transfer conditions make intervention impossible mid-air
options.C: Patient movement is restricted to prevent motion sickness
options.D: Helicopters lack sufficient cabin lighting to see loose equipment

explanation: High winds and noisy environments during hoisting prevent any troubleshooting of dislodged lines. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h6)
